chapter: Records, Blanton, the Chicago scene, Nat Cole and Nadine
title: Warwick Hall and the segregated Chicago unions
summary: On Thursday nights the Musicians' Union held jam nights with Locals 208 and 10 and meager shares.

story.theme_name: The musicians' union: cards, locals, and the Black-white merger
story.community_name: The musicians' union: cards, scale and the black-white merger

blocks.x: Well, this was around early '37 that I played with King Kolax out here. But then I ran into him in Chicago, and they had a hall there, the Warwick Hall. Where all musicians graduated from, like Gene Ammons graduated from there with King Kolax.

But on Thursday nights, Mr. Hall, that owned Warwick Hall would donate the hall to the Musicians' Union. Like, they had segregated unions then. 208 It was a black local, and 10 was the white local. That was Petrillo's union at that time. And they'd have two bands, one on one side of the house and one on the other. And whatever money was made would be split up amongst the musicians. This'll kill you. We'd end up at the end of the night splitting up 35 cents apiece, 50 cents, a quarter. Place be packed. Hall was stealing all the money. Boy, those were some funny times.
